# New renderings — iliad-043 (7.181–282)

Rows for the table in `conventions.md`. Departures from published English: one. 7.201 takes the English of 7.178 (iliad-042); 7.202 that of 3.276 (iliad-019); 7.229–230 that of 2.771–772 (iliad-014), ending at λαῶν with ";" for "·"; 7.251–252, 7.253 and 7.254b are whole units identical to the published ones (3.357–358, 3.359, 3.360 in iliad-019); 7.244 (first line), 7.250 (3.356, with ἐΐσην for ἴσην) and 7.257 reuse the published wording of iliad-019 and iliad-034 inside units whose other lines are new. 7.269 is the Odyssey's line (9.538) with one change: ἶν’ ἀπέλεθρον keeps the Iliad table's "strength immeasurable" / "immeasurable strength" (5.245, which turns "measureless" down) in place of the Odyssey's "measureless"; the Iliad's own row wins over a shared line. 7.245 and 7.266 are the same Greek and have the same English.

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| κοίρανε λαῶν (7.234, vocative) | "ruler of the people" | "ruler of the people" | "lord of the host", "leader of men", "commander" (ἄναξ ἀνδρῶν is "lord of men", ποιμὴν λαῶν "shepherd of the people"); keeps κοίρανος "ruler" |
| Αἶαν διογενὲς Τελαμώνιε (7.234) | "Ajax, Zeus-sprung, Telamonian" | "Zeus-born Ajax, Telamonian" | "Ajax son of Telamon", "scion of Zeus"; the table's διογενής pair "Zeus-sprung" / "Zeus-born" and Τελαμώνιος "Telamonian" |
| Αἴας διογενής (7.249) | "Zeus-sprung Ajax" | "Zeus-born Ajax" | as the row above |
| ἑπταβόειον (σάκος, 7.220, 7.222, 7.245, 7.266) | "seven-hided" | "seven-hided" | "sevenfold", "seven-layered", "of seven ox-hides" (each hides the Greek βόειος "of an ox") |
| δεινὸν σάκος (7.245, 7.266) | "the dread … shield" | "dread … shield" | "terrible", "fearsome" (reserved for αἰνός), "formidable"; δεινός keeps "dread" (1.200) |
| νώροπι χαλκῷ (7.206) | "flashing bronze" | "flashing bronze" (+ note: sense not certain) | "glittering", "gleaming" (γλαυκῶπις), "shining" (φαεινός); the shipped νώροπα χαλκόν "the flashing bronze" (iliad-013, 2.578; Odyssey 24.467), unchanged in the dative; "flashing" is the traditional guess and the formation is not certain |
| θυμοβόρος (ἔριδος, 7.210) | "heart-devouring" | "heart-devouring" | "heart-consuming", "soul-eating", "life-draining"; θυμός "heart" + the root of βιβρώσκω "eat" |
| βλοσυροῖσι προσώπασι (7.212) | "grim faces" | "a grim face" (+ note: some ancient readers took βλοσυρός as 'shaggy') | "fierce", "stern", "shaggy", "bristling" (each decides it); πρόσωπον "face" |
| κραδάων (δολιχόσκιον ἔγχος, 7.213) | "swinging" | "swinging" | "brandishing" (kept for ἀμπεπαλών), "shaking" (σείων), "wielding" (νωμάω, 7.238, where `i` has "wield"), "quivering" |
| τρόμος αἰνός (7.215) | "a fearsome trembling" | "a fearsome trembling" | "dreadful" (reserved for δεινός), "terrible", "grim shudder"; αἰνός "fearsome" (δηΐου … αἰνῆς δηϊοτῆτος, 7.174) |
| ὑπήλυθε γυῖα (7.215) | "crept, upon the limbs of each" | "crept over the limbs of every Trojan" | "ran through", "seized" (τοὺς … ὑπὸ τρόμος εἷλεν is another verb), "went down" |
| προκαλέσσατο χάρμῃ (7.218) | "had challenged in the joy of battle" | "had issued the challenge in the joy of battle" | "to the fight", "to battle"; keeps the table's χάρμη "the joy of battle" (4.222) |
| σκυτοτόμων (7.221) | "leather-cutters" | "leather-workers" | "cobblers", "tanners", "shoemakers" (σκῦτος "leather" + τέμνω "cut", covering all hide-work) |
| Ὕλῃ ἔνι οἰκία ναίων (7.221) | "in Hyle having his home" | "who lived in his home in Hyle" | "dwelling in the house at Hyle"; οἰκία "home" (2.750), ναίω "dwell" |
| αἰόλον (σάκος αἰόλον, 7.222) | "glancing" | "glancing" | "gleaming" (γλαυκῶπις), "bright", "many-coloured" (each decides whether it is the sheen or the colours); the root of κορυθαίολος "of the glancing helmet" |
| ζατρεφέων (ταύρων, 7.223) | "sleek" | "well-fed" | follows the table's ζατρεφέας (4.451) |
| ἤλασε χαλκόν (ἐπὶ δ’ ὄγδοον ἤλασε χαλκόν, 7.223) | "drove … bronze" | "hammered on … a layer, of bronze" | "struck" (ἤλασε of a blow, 19.393), "laid" (no force), "forged" (a stronger claim than the Greek) |
| οἰόθεν οἶος (7.226) | "singly, alone" | "all alone" | the table's row (7.39), unchanged; "one against one", "by himself alone" |
| ῥηξήνωρ (Ἀχιλλῆα ῥηξήνορα, 7.228) | "man-breaking" | "the man-breaker" (+ note: whether ranks or men are broken is not known) | "breaker of ranks", "man-slaying", "who breaks men's lines" (each decides it); ῥήγνυμι "break" + ἀνήρ |
| τοῖοι οἳ ἂν σέθεν ἀντιάσαιμεν (7.231) | "such as might meet you" | "men among us who could face you" | "who could withstand you", "to oppose you"; ἀντιάω "meet, face" |
| ἄρχε μάχης ἠδὲ πτολέμοιο (7.232) | "begin the battle and the war" | "begin the battle and the war" | "lead", "open the fight", "start the fray"; μάχη "battle", πόλεμος "war" |
| μή τί μευ … πειρήτιζε (7.235) | "make trial of me" | "do not make trial of me" | "test", "provoke", "try out"; follows the table's ἐγχείῃ πειρήσομαι "make trial" |
| ἀφαυρός (παιδὸς ἀφαυροῦ, 7.235) | "weak" | "weak" | "feeble" (ἀλαπαδνός), "frail", "puny"; follows ἀφαυροτάτη "the weakest" (20.110) |
| βῶν ἀζαλέην (7.238–239; βοῦς for its hide) | "the dry ox-hide" | "the dry ox-hide" | "dried", "withered", "tough"; ἀζαλέος "dry", the shield being named by its material |
| ταλαύρινον (7.239) | "shield-enduring" | "steadfast in my shield" (+ note: meaning uncertain, perhaps τλάω + ῥινός) | "shield-bearing", "stubborn", "bold in the shield"; `l` follows the table's ταλαύρινος "shield-enduring" (5.289); `i` is not the table's "who bears the hide shield" because the word is a predicate here, and the note says the sense is a guess |
| μόθος (7.240) | "press" | "press" | "tumult", "melee", "din"; ἐπαΐξαι μόθον ἵππων is "to rush upon the press of horses" |
| σταδίη δηΐῳ μέλπεσθαι Ἄρηϊ (7.241) | "in the standing fight to dance for hostile Ares" | "dance the dance of hostile war in the fight where men stand their ground" | "dance in the grim war-dance", "play at war" (loses μέλπω "dance and sing"); Ἄρηϊ is the god in `l` and the war in `i`, as the Iliad table's ξυνάγωμεν Ἄρηα "join battle" |
| λάθρῃ ὀπιπεύσας (7.243) | "by stealth, spying on you" | "by stealth, after watching for my chance" | "from ambush", "secretly" alone, "sneaking"; ὀπιπεύω "look at, watch" |
| ἀμπεπαλὼν προΐει δολιχόσκιον ἔγχος (7.244, with a comma after ῥα printed) | published (iliad-019, 3.355) | published | the table's row, unchanged |
| ἀκρότατον κατὰ χαλκόν (7.246) | "upon the topmost bronze" | "on the topmost bronze" | "outermost", "on the rim"; ἄκρος "topmost" |
| πτύχας (7.247, of the layers of a shield) | "folds" | "folds" | "layers", "plates" (the layers are hide, not metal) |
| δαΐζων … χαλκὸς ἀτειρής (7.247) | "rending, … the unwearied bronze" | "rending them, … the unwearied bronze" | "tearing", "cleaving", "tireless"; ἀτειρέα χαλκόν "the unwearied bronze" (13.368) |
| σχέτο (7.248) | "was stopped" | "was stopped" | "held", "was held fast" (reserved for ἔχω of holding), "was checked" |
| πάντοσ’ ἐΐσην (7.250) | "equal on every side" | "equal on every side" | the table's πάντοσε ἴσην, unchanged (ἐΐση is the longer form of the same word) |
| στυφέλιξε μεμαῶτα (7.261) | "thrust roughly, eager as he was" | "shoved him, eager as he was" | "thrust back", "drove back" (the Greek has no ἀνά- here); keeps the table's στυφελίζω "thrust roughly" / "shove" |
| τμήδην (7.262) | "cutting" | "cut along" | "grazing" (turned down for διάμησε), "slicing", "shearing"; τέμνω "cut" |
| μέλαν … αἷμα (7.262) | "dark blood" | "dark blood" | "black blood"; follows the table's αἷμα κελαινόν "dark blood" |
| μέλανα τρηχύν τε μέγαν τε (λίθον, 7.265) | "black and rough and great" | "black and rough and great" | "dark", "huge" (reserved for πελώριος), "jagged" (ὀκριόεις); τρηχύς "rough" (5.308) |
| μυλοειδέϊ πέτρῳ (7.270) | "the millstone-like rock" | "the rock like a millstone" | "millstone-shaped", "round as a millstone"; μύλη "mill" + -ειδής "like" |
| φίλα γούναθ’ (7.271) | "his dear knees" | "Hector’s knees" (+ note: φίλος possessive "his own") | "his own knees" in `l`, "his beloved knees"; follows the table's καὶ φίλον ἦτορ "dear heart" |
| ἐπομφάλιον (7.267) | "on the boss" | "on the boss" | "at the navel" (the Greek word is ὀμφαλός "boss"), "at the centre of the boss"; ὀμφαλόεσσα ἀσπίς "bossed shield" (4.448) |
| περιήχησεν χαλκός (7.267) | "rang all round" | "rang all around" | "resounded", "clanged", "clashed"; περι- "all round" |
| ἐγχριμφθείς (7.272) | "pressed against" | "driven hard against" | "crushed", "dashed", "squeezed" (each decides how hard); ἐγχρίμπτω "press close" |
| ὤρθωσεν (7.272) | "set upright" | "set … upright" | "raised", "lifted", "healed" (the Greek says Apollo set him on his feet, not that he cured him) |
| Διὸς ἄγγελοι ἠδὲ καὶ ἀνδρῶν (7.274; heralds) | "messengers of Zeus and also of men" | "the messengers of Zeus and of men as well" | the table's 1.334, unchanged |
| πεπνυμένω ἄμφω (7.276) | "the two prudent" | "both prudent men" | the table's 3.148, unchanged ("both prudent" in `l` was the first draft) |
| σκῆπτρα σχέθον (7.277) | "held … sceptres" | "held their sceptres" | "raised", "lifted", "stretched out"; σχέθον "held" (the aorist of ἔχω) |
| κῆρυξ Ἰδαῖος πεπνυμένα μήδεα εἰδώς (7.278) | "the herald Idaeus, prudent counsels knowing" | "the herald Idaeus, a man versed in prudent counsels" | the table's μήδεα εἰδώς row, unchanged |
| παῖδε φίλω (7.279, dual vocative of warriors) | "dear sons" | "Dear sons" | "dear boys", "my children", "good lads"; παῖς "son" here, a herald's term of address, and the note says it is not kinship |
| ἀμφοτέρω … σφῶϊ φιλεῖ (7.280) | "both of you loves" | "loves you both" | "is fond of", "cherishes"; φιλέω "love" |
| ἄμφω δ’ αἰχμητά (7.281) | "and both spearmen" | "and you are both spearmen" | "spear-fighters", "warriors"; the table's αἰχμητής "spearman" (5.197) |
| τό γε δὴ καὶ ἴδμεν ἅπαντες (7.281) | "this indeed we also know, all of us" | "and that we all know" | "we all know that well", "as everyone knows"; ἴδμεν = ἴσμεν "we know" |
| νὺξ … τελέθει (7.282) | "night … is here" | "night is already here" | "is falling", "is coming on", "is beginning" (each decides a process); τελέθω "be, come to be" |
| ἀγαθὸν καὶ νυκτὶ πιθέσθαι (7.282) | "it is good also to obey night" | "it is good to yield to night as well" | "give way to", "heed" (in `l`); πείθομαι "obey" in `l` and "yield to" in `i` |
| ἐγγύθεν ἦλθε (7.219) | "from close by came" | "came up from close by" | "came near", "approached", "came close"; the Odyssey table's ἐγγύθεν ἦλθεν (17.71), unchanged |
| ἶν’ ἀπέλεθρον (7.269 = Odyssey 9.538) | "strength immeasurable" | "immeasurable strength" | "measureless" (the Odyssey's wording at 9.538: a departure from it, because the Iliad table's row 5.245 is the same phrase and turns "measureless" down) |
